findings.claim: Acceptance clause A2, "toFahrenheit rounds its result to the nearest integer", contradicts V-2, "Results are never rounded silently; the caller chooses the precision": A2 fixes the precision with no caller input, and it preserves the Math.round already in convert.ts line 1, while toCelsius in the same file does not round.

The vision says "This arc advances: V-1, V-2, V-3", but the Phase-0 slice lists advances ["V-1"] and the only obligation, I-1, serves only V-1, so no obligation serves V-2 or V-3; I-1's witness of toFahrenheit(100) returning 212 also passes under the current rounding code, and so gives no evidence for V-2.

The census marks T-2 ("toCelsius(32) returns 0") out-of-slice, but V-1 is conversion "between Celsius and Fahrenheit" and A1 requires u-convert to export toCelsius, so the slice needs this rule; as drafted, no obligation or test checks toCelsius behaviour even though the unit lane could check it directly.

I-1 carries a proofJudgment of "proves" for witness test id "convert", but the repository contains no test file, no acceptance clause in u-convert requires one to be written, and there is no package.json or tsconfig, so whether the unit lane's bare `node --test` would discover a TypeScript test and import convert.ts depends on a test file name and Node version the pack does not fix.
The plan says u-convert "implements convert.ts", but that file already exists and already satisfies both A1 and A2, so the spec as written asks for no change to the code.

The rules index places T-1 and T-2 in docs/target.md, but that file is absent from the working directory, so the corpus text and I-1's textSha256 pin cannot be checked against the repository at this head.

The vision lists open question Q-1 on Kelvin with the working assumption "Celsius and Fahrenheit only", but the Phase-0 questions list is empty, so the record does not carry the question or its assumption.

reasons: I read the whole pack and listed every file in the working directory; convert.ts is the only file found, and I read it in full.
A2 is blocking because a spec clause and a vision clause cannot both hold, and the vision decides what the pack is for.
The missing V-2 and V-3 coverage is blocking because the vision says the arc advances three clauses, while the slice and the obligations cover only V-1.
The T-2 census state is blocking because the census method treats out-of-slice for a rule the slice needs as a wrong state, and V-1 and A1 both reach toCelsius.
The test, already-satisfied-unit, missing corpus file and Q-1 items are notes because the pack can still run with them, though each could cost an engineer time or leave the record incomplete.
I did not recompute I-1's textSha256 because the corpus file is absent and I had no tool to hash the text, and I did not run the lane because this review is read-only.
Time and clock checks produced no finding because neither the code nor the pack has any date- or time-dependent behaviour.

premises.claim: toFahrenheit in convert.ts rounds its result with Math.round.
toCelsius in convert.ts is exported and returns (f - 32) * 5 / 9 without rounding.
A file listing of the working directory returned only convert.ts, so it holds no test file, package.json, tsconfig or docs/target.md.
